translationRepairs: Once the enemy had withdrawn, he pressed on toward Thanh Hoa ahead of the others.
Once the enemy had withdrawn, he pressed on toward Tuyen Quang ahead of the others.
s0034 宣光 is Tuyên Quang; Thanh Hoa is 清化. The idiomatic wrongly substitutes Thanh Hoa; the proposed place name matches the Chinese and the following siege at the city gates.
Once the enemy had withdrawn, he pressed on first toward Thanh Hoa.
Once the enemy had withdrawn, he pressed on first toward Tuyen Quang.
s0034 宣光 is Tuyên Quang, not Thanh Hoa (清化); the literal place name must be corrected the same way as the idiomatic.
For the victory at Thanh Hoa he was awarded the peacock feather, granted the title Huogachun Batulu, promoted to second rank, and appointed intendant of the Taiwan circuit in Fujian.
For the victory at Tuyen Quang he was awarded the peacock feather, granted the title Huogachun Batulu, promoted to second rank, and appointed intendant of the Taiwan circuit in Fujian.
s0042 論宣光獲勝功 rewards merit at 宣光 (Tuyên Quang); Thanh Hoa is a different Vietnamese place (清化).
In recognition of the victory at Thanh Hoa he was awarded the peacock feather, granted the title Huogachun Batulu, promoted to second rank, and appointed intendant of Taiwan circuit in Fujian.
In recognition of the victory at Tuyen Quang he was awarded the peacock feather, granted the title Huogachun Batulu, promoted to second rank, and appointed intendant of Taiwan circuit in Fujian.
s0042 宣光 is Tuyên Quang; the literal wrongly renders it as Thanh Hoa and the proposed replacement restores the correct place.

The Vietnamese were afraid and made peace, appointing Yongfu deputy commander of the Three Xuan with jurisdiction over Thanh Hoa, Xinghua, and Son Tay, establishing an office at Baosheng and levying transit duties to help pay the army.

The Vietnamese were afraid and made peace, appointing Yongfu deputy commander of the Three Xuan with jurisdiction over Tuyen Quang, Xinghua, and Son Tay, establishing an office at Baosheng and levying transit duties to help pay the army.
s0074 轄宣光、興化、山西三省 lists 宣光 as the first of the Three Xuan provinces; that is Tuyên Quang, not Thanh Hoa.

The Vietnamese were afraid and made peace, appointing Yongfu deputy commander of the Three Xuan, with jurisdiction over Thanh Hoa, Xinghua, and Son Tay, establishing an office at Baosheng and levying transit duties to help pay the army.

The Vietnamese were afraid and made peace, appointing Yongfu deputy commander of the Three Xuan, with jurisdiction over Tuyen Quang, Xinghua, and Son Tay, establishing an office at Baosheng and levying transit duties to help pay the army.
s0074 宣光 is Tuyên Quang among the three provinces under Yongfu; the literal Thanh Hoa misidentifies the place.
The French harassed Thanh Hoa; Yongfu buried land mines to await them, for days concealed his troops to lure the enemy, and they did not dare come out.
The French harassed Tuyen Quang; Yongfu buried land mines to await them, for days concealed his troops to lure the enemy, and they did not dare come out.
s0100 法人擾宣光 names Tuyên Quang; Thanh Hoa is not in the Chinese and must be replaced.
The French harassed Thanh Hoa; Yongfu buried land mines to await them, for days concealed his troops to lure the enemy, and they did not dare come out.
The French harassed Tuyen Quang; Yongfu buried land mines to await them, for days concealed his troops to lure the enemy, and they did not dare come out.
s0100 宣光 is Tuyên Quang; the literal’s Thanh Hoa is the same place-name error as in the idiomatic.
For victories at Thanh Hoa and Lin Tao he was granted the title Yibode'en Batulu.
For victories at Tuyen Quang and Lin Tao he was granted the title Yibode'en Batulu.
s0106 論勝宣、臨功 abbreviates 宣光 and 臨洮; 宣 is Tuyên Quang, not Thanh Hoa, while 臨 as Lin Tao is already correct.
In recognition of victories at Thanh Hoa and Lin Tao he was granted the title Yibode'en Batulu.
In recognition of victories at Tuyen Quang and Lin Tao he was granted the title Yibode'en Batulu.
s0106 宣 abbreviates 宣光 (Tuyên Quang); the literal Thanh Hoa is wrong and the proposed Tuyen Quang matches the Chinese abbreviation.

Late in the Tongzhi reign the French took Hanoi; the French general Rivière colluded with the Vietnamese bandit Huang Chongying to seize all Vietnam, mustered tens of thousands, and was known as the Yellow Flag.

Late in the Tongzhi reign the French took Hanoi; the French general An Ye (Francis Garnier) colluded with the Vietnamese bandit Huang Chongying to seize all Vietnam, mustered tens of thousands, and was known as the Yellow Flag.
s0071 法將安鄴 is Francis Garnier (安鄴), not Henri Rivière (李威利 elsewhere); the proposed An Ye (Francis Garnier) correctly identifies the person named in the Chinese.

At the end of Tongzhi the French took Hanoi; the French general Rivière colluded with the Vietnamese bandit Huang Chongying to seize all Vietnam, mustered tens of thousands, and was called the Yellow Flag.

At the end of Tongzhi the French took Hanoi; the French general An Ye (Francis Garnier) colluded with the Vietnamese bandit Huang Chongying to seize all Vietnam, mustered tens of thousands, and was called the Yellow Flag.
s0071 names 安鄴, not Rivière; An Ye (Francis Garnier) is the accurate English identification of that French general.
The king of Vietnam ordered Yongfu to return; Yongfu circled to Hanoi, resisted the French, set an ambush to lure and kill Rivière, and destroyed his whole army.
The king of Vietnam ordered Yongfu to return; Yongfu circled to Hanoi, resisted the French, set an ambush to lure and kill An Ye (Francis Garnier), and destroyed his whole army.
s0072 誘斬安鄴 refers to killing 安鄴 (Francis Garnier); the English Rivière is a false identification of the same Chinese name.
The king of Vietnam ordered Yongfu to return; Yongfu then circled to Hanoi, resisted the French, set an ambush to lure and behead Rivière, and destroyed his whole army.
The king of Vietnam ordered Yongfu to return; Yongfu then circled to Hanoi, resisted the French, set an ambush to lure and behead An Ye (Francis Garnier), and destroyed his whole army.
s0072 斬安鄴 is Garnier, not Rivière; the literal must name An Ye (Francis Garnier) to match the Chinese victim of the ambush.
